title: Deceleration magnitude
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the constant deceleration of train B using a kinematic equation with given stopping distance and initial speed.

title: Collision analysis logic
description: Important: Correctly applies the condition for a collision (relative displacement <= initial separation) or finds the time of closest approach.

title: Part 2 displacement
description: Essential: Correctly determines if a collision occurs in part (2) and states the corresponding final numerical answer (collision displacement or minimum distance).

title: Equal speed condition
description: Important: Recognizes that the closest approach in the non-collision scenarios occurs when the velocities of A and B are equal.

title: Part 3 outcome
description: Essential: Correctly determines if a collision is avoided in part (3) and states the corresponding final numerical answer (minimum distance or collision displacement).

title: Sign error in acceleration
description: Pitfall: Uses acceleration with incorrect sign (e.g., positive for deceleration) in kinematic equations.

title: Relative motion setup
description: Important: Correctly sets up the positions of trains A and B relative to a common point (e.g., B's braking point) for displacement comparison.

title: Time delay handling
description: Important: Correctly accounts for the 8-second delay before train A accelerates in part (3).
